Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of England. It will be the duo of Aiden Markram and Ryan Rickelton to open the innings for South Africa. Jofra Archer has the new ball in hand and is raring to go.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The bowling from South Africa was patchy to say the best, but Corbin Bosch did show good control and variety and picked up a couple of wickets, as did Keshav Maharaj. However, their batters now have a tough task at hand as they look to seal a clean sweep. England have the runs on the board but they will need to bowl well as they are still playing three part-timers to make up for the proper fifth bowler. South Africa weren't at their best in the field and bowled way too many wides and with skipper Temba Bavuma being off the field in the last 10 or so overs of the first innings, their batting could be hampered as well. Can they pull off a miracle, though? Only time will tell. Do join us for the run chase which will begin shortly.

Heading into the final phase of the game, South Africa managed to snatch up a couple of wickets as Bethell departed for a fine 110 and Harry Brook departed just a couple of balls later. Jos Buttler then came in and never took his foot off the pedal as Joe Root went on to bring up his 19th ODI ton and got out soon after. Buttler remained unbeaten on 62 off just 32 balls as he hit three boundaries in the space of 4 balls in the final over to hand all the momentum to his team. England have now become the first team to reach 400 twice this year in an ODI - the previous occasion being against West Indies at Edgbaston in May.

Jamie Smith got a life soon after Duckett fell, but made good use of it and stitched together another decent stand with Joe Root before getting out on 62. The score was 117/2 when Jacob Bethell walked in and then came the defining stand of the first innings. Bethell and Root added 182 big runs in just 24 overs as Bethell brought up a maiden ODI century.

After being asked to bat first, England had a blistering start in the first 10 overs. The South African pacers were all over the place and both Jamie Smith and Ben Duckett punished the bad balls. Duckett still looked a bit undercooked and eventually fell as Corbin Bosch handed the visitors their first breakthrough.

England love playing here at the Rose Bowl and for the first time, 400-plus has been scored at this venue in an ODI game. This is also the first time England have crossed the 400-run barrier against South Africa in an ODI game and what a feisty finish that was from Jos Buttler as well. As for the Proteas, they have conceded 400-plus in back-to-back dead rubbers, the previous one was 431 in the third ODI against Australia just a couple of weeks back and this also the 4th time they have conceded over 400 runs, only behind West Indies who have achieved this unwanted feat 5 times.

They appeared to be a full-fledged, relentless batting force after adding Tristan Stubbs, Dewald Brevis, and Matthew Breetzke to the middle order, with Breetzke going on to score a record fifth consecutive score of 50 or more in his first 5 ODIs in the previous game. While expertly leading the spin department, Keshav Maharaj has already taken six wickets in two games, including a four-fer in the opening game. With some encouraging performances from Nandre Burger and Lungi Ngidi, the seam bowlers have done their share without Kagiso Rabada's assistance.

Hello and warm greetings to everyone joining us, as we gear up for the third and final ODI match of the series between England and South Africa held at the Rose Bowl in Southampton. The Proteas have continued their dream run in 2025 and have already taken an unassailable lead of 2-0 in the ODI series against England and eye a whitewash in the third ODI series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The bandwagon rolls into Southampton for the third and final ODI between England and South Africa at the Hampshire Bowl. The Proteas have already wrapped up the series with back-to-back wins. For Temba Bavuma and his men, it has been a year of milestones as they seem to have made a habit of creating history at Lord’s. Earlier in the year, they lifted the World Test Championship mace there and have now followed it up by securing their first bilateral ODI series win in England since 1998. For England, it is yet another setback in a format where their struggles do not seem to end. Since the 2023 ODI World Cup, they have managed to win just one of their six bilateral series in the format. The opener was a one-sided affair, dominated entirely by South Africa, while the second ODI was far more competitive. Chasing 331, the hosts fought hard but fell just six runs short. Looking ahead, Harry Brook and his team will need to reassess their balance after the decision to field only four specialist bowlers backfired at Lord’s. The attempt to fill the fifth bowler’s quota through Will Jacks and Jacob Bethell proved costly, and yet for the third ODI, they have once again opted for just four frontline options. The only change sees Jamie Overton come in for Saqib Mahmood, a move that adds depth with the bat but does little to address the bowling shortfall. On the batting front, the lack of meaningful conversions has been a concern. Harry Brook and Ben Duckett, in particular, have struggled to make an impact and will be eager to change that in Southampton. For South Africa, winning back-to-back ODI series in Australia and now in England without Kagiso Rabada is a remarkable achievement. In his absence, Nandre Burger and Lungi Ngidi have stepped up admirably. Just as vital has been Keshav Maharaj, who continues to underline why he holds the top spot in the ODI bowling rankings. In both matches, Aiden Markram and Ryan Rickelton have provided solid starts, ensuring South Africa avoided early setbacks at the top. Returning at number four after missing the opener with a hamstring concern, Matthew Breetzke picked up right where he left off. He etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter in ODI history to score a half-century in each of his first five innings. With the series already secured, the Proteas might look to rotate their squad for the final game. More history beckons for South Africa, who have never completed a clean sweep against England in an ODI series, either at home or away. For the hosts, the focus will be on salvaging pride and carrying some momentum into the upcoming T20I series. Who are you backing to come out on top?
